steps.title: The season recital
steps.body:
Three months of sittings end here. Two pieces for the family, and one thing you teach.

1. Say the names, play both pieces, hold the last note, bow. Everything you know about recitals is in that sentence.
2. Then teach someone younger a four-note tune. Show it slowly, let them try, fix one thing, let them try again. Teaching it is the proof that you know it.
3. The family asks one question. Answer it.

Then the Practice log, the long version: which trick from this season helped most, and which piece you would still play in a year.

steps.title: Teach someone younger a tune
steps.body: Tick each one before and during recital day.
checklist: Two recital pieces run once a day this week
The four-note tune played slowly for someone younger
They tried it, you fixed one thing, they tried again
Names said, both pieces played, last note held, a bow
The family asked one question, and you answered it

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record the recital in one take: both pieces, names said, hands in the frame. If the lesson went well, add a second clip of the tune being taught.
